Subject: RE: Concierge pilot — order form questions on floors/caps and fallback

Marta — thanks for the clear note and the annotated Order Form.

High-level response: we can accommodate a short pilot-floor carveout and provide a limited-price-freeze fallback with a few guardrails. I've attached a redline of Exhibit B that implements a 2-quarter pilot floor set at 25% of the standard quarterly minimum + a true-up mechanism at the end of Q2. I've also sketched fallback language that:

- Allows Redwood to move Concierge to a nearest-cost-equivalent model variant when a variant is retired;
- Caps per-token price increases for 90 days following any involuntary model change at no more than 10% above the pre-change rate;
- Requires Redwood to notify Concierge 14 days in advance when possible and to provide a compatibility report and automated rollback option if quality regressions exceed the agreed delta.

Caveats for legal: any permanent long-term cap or guaranteed elasticity across versions is tough for us because hardware and quantization choices materially change unit economics. The 90-day buffer + true-up is intended to balance predictability with operational reality.

I'm looping Jordan from Sales (commercial fallback playbook) and Irene from Legal to propose precise redline language. If those edits look acceptable we can package them for a one-time approval signature (DocuSign link below) and commit to CSI monitoring during the pilot.

Attachments: ExhibitB_PricingMatrix_redline.docx
DocuSign (proposal): https://app.docusign.com/packaging/RDW-4521

—Rishi

Marta / team — quick legal check-in. Thanks Rishi for the draft. A few legal redline suggestions to keep contract exposure bounded:

1) Pilot Floor: Accept pilot floor at 25% for two consecutive fiscal quarters but add a one-time option for Concierge to terminate the pilot without penalty if verified usage and integration milestones (listed in SOW) are not met by the end of the second pilot quarter. This prevents premature true-ups for non-integrated pilots.

2) Fallback / Model Retirement: Replace "nearest-cost-equivalent" with "commercially reasonable equivalent" and include an explicit process: (i) notice 14 days, (ii) provide synthetic test vector report comparing outputs, (iii) allow Concierge 7 days to request mitigation (fallback route or cached-output compensation).

3) Temporary Price Cap: The 90-day, 10% cap is acceptable provided it excludes pass-through costs (third-party infra egress/market exchange adjustments) and that a maximum absolute cap is stated for clarity. Suggest language: "not to exceed 10% above the applicable per-token rate on the Effective Date, subject to pass-through adjustments expressly identified in Schedule X."

4) Audit / Quality Delta: Any rollback/compensation triggers must be tied to a measurable delta using the mutually agreed evaluation harness (we can reference the Drive folder linked).

I've attached a short addendum (OrderForm_SLA_addendum.pdf) with the suggested clause language; please review and confirm if Concierge can accept these guardrails or whether Procurement will push for a firmer long-term cap.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
